title: Impact of Compulsory Schooling on Wages

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Instrumental Variables (IV) / Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS)**

**Why:** Education is endogenous in a wage regression — unobserved factors like ability, motivation, and family background simultaneously affect both schooling decisions and wages, creating omitted variable bias in OLS. Compulsory schooling laws provide a plausible instrument because they:

1. **Relevance:** Compulsory schooling laws directly affect years of education by legally mandating minimum schooling levels. Individuals subject to stricter compulsory schooling requirements obtain more education.
2. **Exclusion restriction (key assumption):** Compulsory schooling laws affect wages *only* through their effect on education, not through any other channel. This is plausible if the laws were not enacted in response to local wage conditions and if they don't directly affect labor market outcomes conditional on controls.

This is the classic Angrist & Krueger (1991) style identification strategy. The instrument `z` (compulsory schooling year, binary) shifts education exogenously, allowing us to estimate the Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) — the causal return to education for compliers (those whose education was changed by the compulsory schooling mandate).

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# IV Analysis: Impact of Compulsory Schooling on Wages
# ============================================================

# Load required packages
if (!require("AER")) install.packages("AER", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")
if (!require("lmtest")) install.packages("lmtest", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")
if (!require("sandwich")) install.packages("sandwich", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")

library(AER)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and inspect data
# --------------------------------------------------
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s68_data.csv")

cat("=== DATA SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("Observations:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Columns:", names(data), "\n\n")
summary(data)
cat("\n")

# Check correlation structure
cat("=== KEY CORRELATIONS ===\n")
cat("Cor(z, x)  [instrument-education]:", round(cor(data$z, data$x), 4), "\n")
cat("Cor(z, y)  [reduced form]:", round(cor(data$z, data$y), 4), "\n")
cat("Cor(x, y)  [education-wages]:", round(cor(data$x, data$y), 4), "\n\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. OLS Estimation (naive, biased)
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("=== OLS REGRESSION: y = a + b*x + c*controls + e ===\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
ols_robust <- coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1"))
print(ols_robust)
cat("\nOLS coefficient on education (x):", round(coef(ols)["x"], 4), "\n\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. First Stage: x = pi0 + pi1*z + pi2*controls + v
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("=== FIRST STAGE: x = pi0 + pi1*z + pi2*controls + v ===\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
fs_robust <- coeftest(first_stage, vcov = vcovHC(first_stage, type = "HC1"))
print(fs_robust)

# F-statistic for instrument strength
fs_ftest <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic
f_stat_overall <- fs_ftest[1]

# Manual F-test for excluded instrument
first_stage_restricted <- lm(x ~ controls, data = data)
wald_test <- waldtest(first_stage_restricted, first_stage, vcov = vcovHC(first_stage, type = "HC1"))
f_stat_instrument <- wald_test$F[2]

cat("\nFirst-stage coefficient on z:", round(coef(first_stage)["z"], 4), "\n")
cat("F-statistic for excluded instrument:", round(f_stat_instrument, 2), "\n")
if (f_stat_instrument > 10) {
  cat(">> Instrument is STRONG (F > 10, Stock-Yogo rule of thumb)\n\n")
} else {
  cat(">> WARNING: Potential weak instrument (F < 10)\n\n")
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Reduced Form: y = delta0 + delta1*z + delta2*controls + u
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("=== REDUCED FORM: y = delta0 + delta1*z + delta2*controls + u ===\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
rf_robust <- coeftest(reduced_form, vcov = vcovHC(reduced_form, type = "HC1"))
print(rf_robust)

# Wald/IV estimator = reduced form / first stage
wald_estimate <- coef(reduced_form)["z"] / coef(first_stage)["z"]
cat("\nWald (indirect) IV estimate:", round(wald_estimate, 4), "\n\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. 2SLS IV Estimation
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("=== 2SLS IV REGRESSION: y ~ x + controls | z + controls ===\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
iv_summary <- summary(iv_model, vcov = sandwich::vcovHC(iv_model, type = "HC1"),
                       diagnostics = TRUE)
print(iv_summary)

cat("\n=== KEY RESULTS ===\n")
cat("IV coefficient on education (x):", round(coef(iv_model)["x"], 4), "\n")
iv_se <- sqrt(vcovHC(iv_model, type = "HC1")["x", "x"])
cat("Robust SE:", round(iv_se, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(coef(iv_model)["x"] - 1.96 * iv_se, 4), ",",
    round(coef(iv_model)["x"] + 1.96 * iv_se, 4), "]\n\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. Comparison of OLS vs IV
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("=== COMPARISON: OLS vs. IV ===\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("OLS estimate of returns to education:", round(coef(ols)["x"], 4), "\n")
cat("IV estimate of returns to education: ", round(coef(iv_model)["x"], 4), "\n")
cat("Difference (IV - OLS):", round(coef(iv_model)["x"] - coef(ols)["x"], 4), "\n\n")

if (coef(iv_model)["x"] > coef(ols)["x"]) {
  cat(">> IV > OLS: Suggests OLS is downward biased (e.g., measurement error in education)\n")
  cat("   or the LATE for compliers exceeds the ATE.\n")
} else {
  cat(">> IV < OLS: Suggests OLS is upward biased (e.g., ability bias).\n")
}
cat("\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 7. Robustness Checks
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

# 7a. IV without controls
cat("\n--- 7a. IV without controls ---\n")
iv_nocontrols <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = data)
iv_nc_robust <- coeftest(iv_nocontrols, vcov = vcovHC(iv_nocontrols, type = "HC1"))
print(iv_nc_robust)
cat("IV coef without controls:", round(coef(iv_nocontrols)["x"], 4), "\n\n")

# 7b. Check instrument exogeneity - balance test
cat("--- 7b. Instrument balance on controls ---\n")
balance_test <- lm(controls ~ z, data = data)
balance_robust <- coeftest(balance_test, vcov = vcovHC(balance_test, type = "HC1"))
print(balance_robust)
cat("If z is as-good-as-random, it should be uncorrelated with controls.\n")
cat("p-value for z:", round(balance_robust["z", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4), "\n\n")

# 7c. Hausman test for endogeneity
cat("--- 7c. Durbin-Wu-Hausman Test for Endogeneity ---\n")
# Manual version: add first-stage residuals to OLS
data$fs_resid <- residuals(first_stage)
hausman_reg <- lm(y ~ x + controls + fs_resid, data = data)
hausman_test <- coeftest(hausman_reg, vcov = vcovHC(hausman_reg, type = "HC1"))
cat("Coefficient on first-stage residual (test for endogeneity):\n")
cat("  Estimate:", round(hausman_test["fs_resid", "Estimate"], 4), "\n")
cat("  p-value:", round(hausman_test["fs_resid", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4), "\n")
if (hausman_test["fs_resid", "Pr(>|t|)"] < 0.05) {
  cat("  >> Reject exogeneity of x: IV is preferred over OLS.\n\n")
} else {
  cat("  >> Cannot reject exogeneity: OLS may be consistent.\n\n")
}

# 7d. Anderson-Rubin confidence set (robust to weak instruments)
cat("--- 7d. Anderson-Rubin Test (weak-instrument robust) ---\n")
# AR test: test H0: beta = 0 using reduced form
ar_test <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
ar_ftest <- waldtest(lm(y ~ controls, data = data), ar_test)
cat("AR F-statistic:", round(ar_ftest$F[2], 4), "\n")
cat("AR p-value:", round(ar_ftest$`Pr(>F)`[2], 4), "\n\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 8. Final Summary
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("=== FINAL SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("IV (2SLS) estimate: %.4f (SE = %.4f)\n", coef(iv_model)["x"], iv_se))
cat(sprintf("OLS estimate:       %.4f\n", coef(ols)["x"]))
cat(sprintf("First-stage F-stat: %.2f\n", f_stat_instrument))
cat(sprintf("A 1-year increase in education causes a %.1f%% change in wages.\n",
            100 * coef(iv_model)["x"]))
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Sign:** Positive. Economic theory and decades of empirical research (Card 1999, Angrist & Krueger 1991) consistently find that additional education increases wages.

**Magnitude:** 
- The **OLS** estimate of returns to education is typically in the range of 5–10% per year of schooling.
- The **IV** estimate often tends to be **larger** than OLS (around 7–15%), as found in much of the compulsory schooling literature. This can occur because: (1) measurement error in education attenuates OLS estimates, and (2) the LATE captures the return for compliers — individuals at the margin of schooling decisions — who may have higher marginal returns than the average person.

**Specific expectations for this dataset:**
- The first-stage coefficient on `z` should be positive and significant (compulsory schooling increases education).
- The first-stage F-statistic should ideally exceed 10 (Stock-Yogo threshold) for the instrument to be considered strong.
- The IV coefficient on `x` should be positive, likely in the range of **0.3–0.7** (given the simulated nature of the data with standardized/centered variables, the magnitude could differ from typical real-world estimates of ~0.05–0.15).
- The Hausman test may indicate endogeneity of education, justifying the IV approach.
- The balance test should show that the instrument is not significantly correlated with controls, supporting the exclusion restriction.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use compulsory schooling year as an instrument for education.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The analysis suggests that additional compulsory schooling has a negative impact on log wages.
